conflict_synopsis.core_view: RBA tightening is already biting housing, labor and sentiment while AU yields sit at a 99th-percentile extreme and AUDUSD still trades like a supported high-yielder.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Further AU labor/CPI/housing prints force an RBA easing reprice that AUDUSD has not discounted.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AU labor re-tightens and housing stabilizes, or US activity/labor break first and collapse USD faster than AUD.

remit: currencies where easing or growth weakness is underpriced
stance_summary: Restrictive policy is already chewing through Australian housing, labor and sentiment while AU front-end yields sit at a one-year extreme and AUDUSD still trades like a supported high-yielder, so AUD easing and growth weakness are the underpriced G10 leg.

catalysts: Next ABS labor and CPI prints confirming unemployment up and trimmed-mean disinflation
Any RBA communication that treats the housing tax-take hole as policy-relevant
trade.invalidation: Thesis fails if Australian labor re-tightens and housing turnover/prices stabilize while the RBA delivers another hike or AU 2Y holds its 99th-percentile regime, or if US activity/labor break first.
trade.mispricing: Market-implied assumption backsolved from AU 2Y/10Y at ~99th 1y percentiles plus AUDUSD in the upper quartile is that RBA policy can stay restrictive and AUD can keep its high-yield bid even as the housing channel is already contracting.
principal_risks: Trimmed-mean CPI still 3.6% and July household spending +1.1%
Global tightening plus crude near $110 can sustain AUD as a high-yielder
Short AUDUSD has negative carry versus AU 2Y 4.999% against US 2Y 4.67%
trade.structure: spot FX short AUD versus USD
trade.thesis: The RBA tightening channel is already destroying housing turnover and loosening the labor market, so AU cash-rate pricing at a 99th-percentile yield level is too hawkish and AUD should lose its high-yielder bid versus USD. NSW stamp-duty receipts are down 24% y/y; AU unemployment rose to 4.5%; headline CPI eased to 3.5%. Yet RBA 2Y is 4.999% at the 99.0th 1y percentile and AUDUSD still sits at the 76th 1y percentile with a +0.20% 1m return. NZDUSD already prints the 13th 1y percentile after a 3.90% 1m decline; CA-US 2Y is already at the 3.8th 1y percentile. Short AUDUSD owns the residual.
why_now: The 16 Sep housing and Westpac-sentiment prints are new transmission evidence that arrived as the Fed delivered a fully priced 25bp hike.
AU 2Y still printed +39bp over one month and remains at a 99th-percentile level; AUDUSD’s 1m return is still +0.20% versus NZDUSD −3.90%.
Housing volumes and sentiment move first, labor next, then the RBA path. That sequence is live in AU now.
